verbatim_text: Intermediaries shall adhere to these guidelines for avoiding or dealing with or managing conflict of interest. They shall be responsible for educating their associated persons for compliance of these guidelines.

title: Define Conflict of Interest Policies and Procedures
summary: Intermediaries must define policies and procedures to identify, avoid or manage actual or potential conflict of interest.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Develop and implement policies and internal procedures to identify, avoid or manage actual or potential conflict of interest.
evidence: Policies and procedures document, communication records to all concerned.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, i. lay down, with active involvement of senior management, policies and internal procedures to identify and avoid or to deal or manage actual or potential conflict of interest, develop an internal code of conduct governing operations and formulate standards of appropriate conduct in the performance of their activities, and ensure to communicate such policies, procedures and code to all concerned;

title: Maintain High Standards of Integrity
summary: Intermediaries must maintain high standards of integrity in the conduct of their business.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Maintain high standards of integrity at all times.
evidence: Internal audit reports, compliance records.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, ii. at all times maintain high standards of integrity in the conduct of their business;

title: Ensure Fair Treatment of Clients
summary: Intermediaries must ensure fair treatment of clients and not discriminate amongst them.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Ensure fair treatment of all clients and avoid discrimination.
evidence: Client feedback, internal review reports.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, iii. ensure fair treatment of their clients and not discriminate amongst them;

title: Prioritize Client Interest
summary: Intermediaries must prioritize client interest over personal interest in all advice, investment decisions, and transactions.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Ensure that personal interest does not conflict with client’s interest in all advice, investment decisions, and transactions.
evidence: Client records, transaction logs.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, iv. ensure that their personal interest does, at any time conflict with their duty to their clients and client’s interest always takes primacy in their advice, investment decisions and transactions;

title: Implement Information Barriers
summary: Intermediaries must implement information barriers to reduce opportunities for conflict.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Implement prescriptive measures such as information barriers to block or hinder the flow of information from one department/unit to another.
evidence: Information barrier policies, communication logs.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, vii. place appropriate restrictions on transactions in securities while handling a mandate of issuer or client in respect of such security so as to avoid any conflict;

title: Avoid Dealing with Material Non-Published Information
summary: Intermediaries must not deal in securities while in possession of material non-published information.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Avoid dealing in securities when possessing material non-published information.
evidence: Transaction records, internal audit reports.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, viii. not deal in securities while in possession of material non published information;

title: Avoid Disclosing Material Non-Published Information
summary: Intermediaries must not disclose material non-published information to others.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Avoid disclosing material non-published information while dealing in securities on behalf of others.
evidence: Transaction records, internal audit reports.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, ix. not to communicate the material non published information while dealing in securities on behalf of others;

title: Avoid Market Manipulation
summary: Intermediaries must avoid contributing to market manipulation or influencing prices of securities.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Avoid any action that may contribute to market manipulation or influence prices of securities.
evidence: Transaction records, internal audit reports.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, x. not in any way contribute to manipulate the demand for or supply of securities in the market or to influence prices of securities;

title: Avoid Incentive Structures Encouraging Unsuitable Products
summary: Intermediaries must avoid incentive structures that encourage sale of products not suitable for clients based on their risk profile.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Ensure that incentive structures do not encourage sale of products unsuitable for clients based on their risk profile.
evidence: Incentive structure policies, client records.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, xi. not have an incentive structure that encourages sale of products not suitable the risk profile of their clients;

title: Prohibit Sharing Client Information for Personal Gain
summary: Intermediaries must not share information received from clients or pertaining to them, obtained as a result of dealings, for personal gain.
trigger: On the lines of Principle 8 of IOSCO Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulations
required_action: Prohibit sharing of client information received from clients or pertaining to them, obtained as a result of dealings, for personal gain.
evidence: Client records, internal audit reports.
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, xii. not share information received from clients or pertaining to them, obtained as a result of their dealings, for their personal interest;

title: Ensure free access to data for users
summary: IAs must ensure that data provided by various data sources in Indian securities markets is made available to users free of charge.
required_action: Make data available for viewing and downloading, as well as usage for value addition purposes, free of cost.
evidence: Documentation of data access policies and procedures ensuring free availability.
verbatim_text: "As far as the data provided by various data sources in Indian securities markets pursuant to regulatory mandates for reporting and disclosure in public domain are concerned, such data should be made available to users, ‘free of charge’ both for ‘viewing’ the data as also for download in the format as specified by regulatory mandate for reporting, as well as their usage for the value addition purposes.”

title: Identify and disclose chargeable data
summary: IAs must appropriately identify and disclose data that is chargeable.
required_action: Appropriately identify and disclose data which is chargeable in the public domain.
evidence: Documentation of identification and disclosure procedures for chargeable data.
verbatim_text: "Further, apart from the data made available free of cost, data which is chargeable should be appropriately identified as such in public domain."

title: Comply with AML and CFT standards
summary: IAs must comply with the guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Standards and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT).
trigger: Regulatory mandates for AML and CFT
required_action: Refer to the specified circulars for guidelines on AML and CFT.
evidence: Documentation of compliance with AML and CFT standards, including adherence to relevant circulars.
verbatim_text: IAs are advised to refer to the following circulars with respect to ‘Guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Standards and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) /Obligations of Securities Market Intermediaries under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and Rules framed there under’ : i. Master Circular issued on June 06, 2024 available at the following link: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/master-circulars/jun-2024/guidelines-on-anti-money-laundering-aml-standards-and-combating-the-financing-of-terrorism-cft-obligations-of-securities-market-intermediaries-under-the-prevention-of-money-laundering-act-2002-a-_83942.html

title: Comply with norms for sharing real-time price data
summary: IAs must comply with the norms for sharing real-time price data to third parties.
required_action: Refer to the specified circulars for guidelines on sharing real-time price data.
evidence: Documentation of compliance with norms for sharing real-time price data, including adherence to relevant circulars.
verbatim_text: IAs are advised to refer to circular no. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2024/56 dated May 24, 2024 on ‘Norms for sharing of real time price data to third parties’ available at: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/may-2024/norms-for-sharing-of-real-time-price-data-to-third-parties_83572.html

title: Include all forms of communications in advertisement
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must include all forms of communication that may influence investment decisions.
required_action: Ensure the communication includes all relevant details and complies with SEBI regulations.
evidence: Records of communications sent, including content and date.
source_clause: i. Advertisement shall include all forms of communications, issued by or on behalf of IA, that may influence investment decisions of any investor or prospective investor.
verbatim_text: Advertisement shall include all forms of communications, issued by or on behalf of IA, that may influence investment decisions of any investor or prospective investor.

title: Specify applicable forms of communication in advertisement code
summary: IAs must specify the types of communications covered by the advertisement code.
required_action: Ensure all specified forms of communication are included in advertisements.
evidence: Records of communications sent, including content and date.
source_clause: ii. The forms of communications, to which the advertisement code shall be applicable, shall include pamphlets, circulars, brochures, notices, research reports or any other literature, document, information or material published, or designed for use in any publication or displays (such as newspaper, magazine, sign boards/hoardings at any location), in any electronic, wired or wireless communication (such as electronic mail, text messaging, messaging platforms, social media platforms, radio, telephone, or in any other form over the internet) or over any other audio-visual form of communication (such as television, tape recording, video tape recordings, motion pictures) or in any other manner whatsoever.
verbatim_text: The forms of communications, to which the advertisement code shall be applicable, shall include pamphlets, circulars, brochures, notices, research reports or any other literature, document, information or material published, or designed for use in any publication or displays (such as newspaper, magazine, sign boards/hoardings at any location), in any electronic, wired or wireless communication (such as electronic mail, text messaging, messaging platforms, social media platforms, radio, telephone, or in any other form over the internet) or over any other audio-visual form of communication (such as television, tape recording, video tape recordings, motion pictures) or in any other manner whatsoever.

title: Submit periodic reports for half-yearly periods
summary: Investment Advisers must submit periodic reports to SEBI within 30 days from the end of each half-yearly period.
trigger: Half-yearly periods ending on September 30 and March 31
required_action: Submit periodic report in the specified format within 30 days from the end of each half-yearly period.
evidence: Periodic reports submitted to SEBI in the specified format.
deadline: within 30 days from the end of the respective half-yearly period
verbatim_text: IAs shall submit periodic report for half-yearly periods ending on September 30 and March 31 of every financial year, within 30 days from the end of the respective half-yearly period for which details are to be furnished.

title: Submit undertaking on compliance with SEBI circulars
summary: Investment Advisers must submit an undertaking regarding the compliance of advisory for Financial Sector Organizations regarding Software as a Service (SaaS) based solutions.
required_action: Submit an undertaking to SEBI confirming compliance with the SEBI circulars.
evidence: Undertaking submitted to SEBI.
verbatim_text: The compliance of the advisory shall be reported by IA to SEBI with an undertaking, “Compliance of the SEBI circular for Advisory for Financial Sector Organizations regarding Software as a Service (SaaS) based solutions has been made.”

title: Annual Audit of Compliance with IA Regulations
summary: Conduct an annual audit in compliance with the IA regulations and submit a report along with any adverse findings within one month from the date of the audit report, but not later than October 31st of each year.
trigger: At the end of each financial year
required_action: Conduct an annual audit and submit a report with adverse findings if any, along with action taken thereof.
evidence: Audit report and action taken report submitted to SEBI within the deadline.
verbatim_text: In terms of regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations, IA is required to conduct annual audit in respect of compliance with the IA regulations and circulars issued thereunder from a member of Institute of Chartered Accountants of India or Institute of Company Secretaries of India within six months from the end of each financial year. Submit a report of the same and adverse findings of the audit, if any, along with action taken thereof duly approved by the individual IA/management of the non-individual IA within a period of one month from the date of the audit report but not later than October 31st of each year for the previous financial year.

title: Incorporate Terms and Conditions in Investment Advisory Agreement
summary: Ensure that specific terms and conditions are incorporated in the Investment Advisory Agreement.
trigger: When entering into an investment advisory agreement with a client
required_action: Incorporate specified terms and conditions in the agreement.
evidence: Copies of signed agreements showing incorporation of required terms and conditions.
verbatim_text: Investment Adviser shall ensure that the following terms and conditions are incorporated in the Investment Advisory Agreement:

title: Client Consent for Services
summary: Obtain client consent to provide investment advisory services, including understanding of fees and mechanisms.
trigger: Before providing any investment advisory services
required_action: Ensure the client has read and understood the terms and conditions along with fee structure and mechanism for charging and payment of fees, and provide an opportunity to ask questions.
evidence: Signed agreement showing consent from the client.
verbatim_text: a) the consent of the client on the following understanding:

title: Investment Adviser Declaration in Agreement
summary: Make specific declarations regarding services, fees, and risk management.
trigger: Before providing any investment advisory services
required_action: Make the specified declarations in the agreement.
evidence: Signed agreement showing the required declarations.
verbatim_text: b) Declaration from the Investment Adviser that:

title: Specify Fees in Agreement
summary: Specify fees and mechanisms for charging and payment of fees.
trigger: Before providing any investment advisory services
required_action: Specify the fees and mechanism for charging and payment of fees in the agreement.
evidence: Signed agreement showing specified fees and mechanisms.
verbatim_text: c) Fees specified under Investment Adviser Regulations and relevant circulars issued thereunder. (to be specifically mentioned here)

title: Specify Fees Charged in Agreement
summary: Specify the fees charged to the client.
trigger: Before providing any investment advisory services
required_action: Specify the fees charged to the client in the agreement.
evidence: Signed agreement showing specified fees charged to the client.
verbatim_text: d) Fees charged to the client. (to be specifically mentioned here)

title: Compliance with SEBI Regulations and Amendments
summary: Investment Advisers must comply with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 and its amendments.
required_action: Accept terms and conditions specified in the regulations.
evidence: Records of compliance with SEBI Regulations and Amendments.
verbatim_text: Terms of compliance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 and its amendments, rules, circulars and notifications.

title: Compliance with Eligibility Criteria
summary: Investment Advisers must comply with the eligibility criteria as specified under the Investment Adviser Regulations at all times.
required_action: Maintain compliance with SEBI's eligibility criteria.
evidence: Records of compliance with SEBI's eligibility criteria.
verbatim_text: Compliance with the eligibility criteria as specified under the Investment Adviser Regulations at all times.

title: Risk Assessment of Clients
summary: Investment Advisers must conduct a risk assessment procedure for their clients, including their risk capacity and risk aversion.
trigger: At the time of onboarding and periodically thereafter as per SEBI guidelines.
required_action: Conduct risk assessments for all clients.
evidence: Risk assessment reports and records.
verbatim_text: Risk assessment procedure of client including their risk capacity and risk aversion.

title: Providing Reports to Clients
summary: Investment Advisers must provide reports to clients on potential and current investments.
trigger: On request or as per SEBI guidelines.
required_action: Provide investment reports to clients.
evidence: Client investment reports.
verbatim_text: Providing reports to clients on potential and current investments.

title: Record Keeping
summary: Investment Advisers must maintain records related to their services, including KYC, risk assessment, analysis reports, suitability, terms and conditions document, books of accounts, and client register.
required_action: Maintain detailed records as specified in the regulations.
evidence: Client-wise KYC documents, risk assessment reports, analysis reports, suitability assessments, terms and conditions document, books of accounts, client register.
verbatim_text: Maintenance of records i.e. client-wise KYC, risk assessment, analysis reports of investment advice and suitability, terms and conditions document, related books of accounts and a register containing list of clients along with Page 55 of 94 dated investment advice and its rationale in compliance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

title: Code of Conduct Compliance
summary: Investment Advisers must abide by the Code of Conduct as specified in the Third Schedule of SEBI regulations.
required_action: Abide by the Code of Conduct.
evidence: Records of adherence to the Code of Conduct.
verbatim_text: Undertaking to abide by the Code of Conduct as specified in the Third Schedule of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

title: Provide termination notice for voluntary agreement termination
summary: Investment Adviser must provide a 30 days prior written notice to the client in case of voluntary termination.
trigger: Voluntary termination of the agreement by Investment Adviser
required_action: Provide a 30 days prior written notice to the client
evidence: Written notice provided to the client
verbatim_text: In case of a voluntary termination of the agreement, the client would be required to give a 30 days prior written notice while the Investment Adviser would be required to give a 30 days prior written notice.

title: Provide option for termination in case of certificate suspension
summary: Investment Adviser must provide an option to the client to terminate the agreement if their certificate is suspended.
trigger: Suspension of the certificate of registration of the Investment Adviser by SEBI
required_action: Provide an option to the client for termination
evidence: Written notice or communication from the Investment Adviser to the client
verbatim_text: In case of suspension of the certificate of registration of the IA, the client may be provided with the option to terminate the agreement.

title: Provide details on implications of amendments and termination
summary: Investment Adviser must provide detailed implications of amendments, terminations, and assignments.
trigger: Amendment or termination of the agreement
required_action: Provide details on set off of fees, refund of fees, completion/termination of investment-in-progress, transition support obligations, etc.
evidence: Written document outlining the implications provided to the client
verbatim_text: The implications of Amendment, Termination and assignment, such as set off of fees received by the Investment Adviser, refund of fees, completion/termination of investment-in-progress, transition support obligations of the Investment Adviser, etc. shall also be provided in detail.

title: Declare independent relationship with related parties
summary: Investment Adviser must declare that it is carrying on its activities independently and disclose any conflicts of interest.
required_action: Declare independence from related parties and disclose any conflicts of interest
evidence: Written declaration or disclosure document
verbatim_text: The Investment Adviser to clearly declare that it is carrying on its activities independently, at an arms-length basis with its related parties. Disclosures of conflicts to be made.

title: Maintain arm's length relationship in other activities (individuals)
summary: Individual Investment Advisers must maintain an arms-length relationship between their investment advisory and other activities.
required_action: Maintain arm's length relationship with related activities
evidence: Written declaration or policy document
verbatim_text: The Investment Adviser (individual) to represent to the client that it maintains an arms-length relationship between its activities as an investment adviser and other activities and to covenant that this arm’s length relationship shall be maintained throughout the tenure of advisory service;

title: Not provide distribution services (individuals)
summary: Individual Investment Advisers must not provide any distribution services.
required_action: Do not provide distribution services
evidence: Written declaration or policy document
verbatim_text: (a) to represent that they shall not provide any distribution services.

title: Not provide investment advisory services to clients receiving distribution from family members (individuals)
summary: Individual Investment Advisers must not provide investment advisory services to a client who is receiving distribution services from other family members.
required_action: Do not provide investment advisory services to clients receiving distribution from family members
evidence: Written declaration or policy document
verbatim_text: (c) to represent that they shall not provide investment advisory services, for securities and investment products, to a client who is receiving distribution services from other family members;

title: Not provide distribution or investment advisory services (non-individuals)
summary: Non-individual Investment Advisers must not provide any distribution or investment advisory services, either directly or through their group.
required_action: Do not provide distribution or investment advisory services to clients or distribution clients
evidence: Written declaration or policy document
verbatim_text: (a) to represent that they shall not provide any distribution services, for securities and investment products, either directly or through their group to an advisory client. (b) to represent that they shall not provide investment advisory services, for securities and investment products, either directly or through their group to the distribution client.

title: Ensure all consents before undertaking actions related to securities or investment product advised by IA
summary: Investment Adviser must obtain all necessary consents and permissions from the client prior to taking any action.
trigger: Undertaking any action in relation to a securities or investment product advised by the Investment Adviser
required_action: Obtain all necessary consents and permissions from the client
evidence: Client consent documents
verbatim_text: The investment adviser to ensure that it will take all consents and permissions from the client prior to undertaking any actions in relation to the securities or investment product advised by the investment adviser.

title: Decline right to seek Power of Attorney
summary: Investment Adviser must clearly declare that it shall not seek a Power of Attorney.
required_action: Decline right to seek Power of Attorney
evidence: Written declaration or policy document
verbatim_text: The Investment Adviser to clearly declare that it shall not seek Power of Attorney:

title: No Action in Relation to Securities or Investment Products
summary: Investment Advisers must not take any actions related to the securities or investment products advised.
trigger: Any action taken by an IA in relation to the securities or investment product advised.
required_action: Avoid taking any such actions.
evidence: Documentation showing no actions were taken.
verbatim_text: No actions in relation to the securities or investment product advised by the investment adviser.

title: Maintain Client Accounts and Data
summary: Investment Advisers must maintain client accounts and data as mandated under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.
trigger: Maintenance of client accounts and data.
required_action: Comply with the regulations for maintaining client accounts and data.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with SEBI regulations.
verbatim_text: Maintenance of accounts and confidentiality: Investment Adviser shall be responsible for maintenance of client accounts and data as mandated under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

title: Provide Specific Details on Fees
summary: Investment Advisers must provide specific details about the fees for investment advice rendered.
trigger: Rendering of investment advice and associated fee arrangements.
required_action: Attach a detailed fee schedule to the agreement, illustrate how fees are determined, specify payment methods, and provide evidence of receipt.
evidence: Fee schedule attached to the agreement, documentation showing payment received.
verbatim_text: Provide specific details on the following: (a) The quantum and manner of payment of fees for investment advice rendered. (i) The quantum and manner of payment of fees for investment advice rendered. (ii) Fee modalities and periodicity, by attaching a detailed fee schedule to the agreement; (iii) Illustration(s) on how the fee will be determined; (iv) whether payment to be made in advance; (v) type of documents evidencing receipt of payment of fee; (vi) Periodicity of billing with clear date and service period

title: Payment of Fees Through Traceable Mode
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure fees are paid through a traceable mode, such as account payee crossed cheque, demand draft, or direct credit.
trigger: Receiving payment of fees from clients.
required_action: Accept payments only via specified traceable modes and not in cash.
evidence: Payment receipts showing traceability of funds.
verbatim_text: The payment of fees shall be through a mode which shows traceability of funds. Such modes may include account payee crossed cheque/ Demand Drafts or by way of direct credit to the bank accounts through NEFT/ RTGS/ IMPS/ UPI or any other mode specified by SEBI from time to time. However, the fees shall not be accepted in cash.

title: Include Liability Statement in Agreement
summary: Investment Advisers must include a statement in their agreement that they will not incur any liability for losses due to market fluctuations or underperformance.
required_action: Clearly state the non-incurring of liability by the IA.
evidence: Agreement with a clear statement regarding non-liability.
verbatim_text: Liability of Investment Adviser: The agreement to clearly state that the Investment Adviser shall not incur any liability by reason of any loss, which a client may suffer by reason of any depletion in the value of the assets under advice, which may result by reason of fluctuation in asset value, or by reason of non-performance or underperformance of the securities/funds or any other market conditions.

title: Make Adequate Representations and Covenants
summary: Investment Advisers must make adequate representations about their qualifications, approvals, and maintain them throughout the validity of advisory services.
trigger: Execution or renewal of advisory service agreements.
required_action: Provide accurate representations and covenants regarding qualifications, approvals, and other relevant matters.
evidence: Documentation showing accurate representations and covenants.
verbatim_text: Representations and covenants: Adequate and appropriate representations about qualifications of the adviser, principal officer, persons associated with the investment advice, receipt of all applicable approvals and consents (from regulatory / statutory bodies, third party consents, corporate approvals etc.) and covenant to maintain them throughout the validity of advisory service.

title: Provisions for Client's Death or Disability
summary: Investment Advisers must include provisions in their agreement regarding continuation or termination of advisory services upon the client’s death or disability.
required_action: Incorporate specific provisions for handling such events.
evidence: Agreement with relevant provisions included.
verbatim_text: Death or Disability of client: Provisions in relation to continuation / termination of the advisory service in event of client's death / disability, succession, nomination, representation etc. to be incorporated.

title: Appoint Obligor for Death or Disability
summary: Investment Advisers must appoint a legal heir, executor, trustee, administrator of the deceased’s estate as the person-in-charge in case of death or disability.
trigger: Death or disability of an IA.
required_action: Appoint one of its legal heirs, executor, trustee, administrator of the deceased’s estate as the person-in-charge.
evidence: Agreement with details of the appointed Obligor.
verbatim_text: Death or Disability of investment adviser: Every individual investment adviser must appoint one of its legal heirs, executor, trustee, administrator of estate of the deceased (the “Obligor”) as the person-in-charge in the event of investment adviser’s death / disability. The agreement must set out the full name, PAN and contact details of such Obligor.

title: Identify and appoint a person-in-charge in case of death/disability
summary: The Investment Adviser must identify and appoint a person-in-charge to take over their responsibilities in the event of their death or disability.
required_action: Identify, appoint, and document the full name, PAN, and contact details of the person-in-charge. Set out steps for taking charge over in case of eventuality.
evidence: Signed agreement with the appointed person-in-charge detailing their responsibilities and contact information.
verbatim_text: The agreement must set out the full name, PAN and contact details of such Obligor. The agreement must disclose the steps to be taken by the Obligor in the event of the above eventuality in order to ensure protection of interest of the clients and redressal of clients’ claims.

title: Set up mechanisms for dispute resolution including arbitration
summary: The Investment Adviser must establish adequate provisions for protecting acts done in good faith and setting up a mechanism for resolving disputes, which may include arbitration.
trigger: Disputes arise between the IA and clients
required_action: Establish mechanisms to protect acts done in good faith and set up a dispute resolution mechanism including arbitration as per SEBI regulations.
evidence: Documentation of established dispute resolution procedures, including any agreements or policies related to arbitration.
verbatim_text: Adequate provisions to cover protection of acts done in good faith as well as for dispute resolution mechanism including arbitration that may be specified under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

title: Resolve client grievances within specified timelines
summary: The Investment Adviser must resolve client grievances within the timelines specified by SEBI circulars.
required_action: Resolve client grievances within the timelines specified under SEBI circulars.

title: Comprehensive Outsourcing Policy
summary: Investment Advisers must have a comprehensive policy in place for assessing whether and how activities can be appropriately outsourced.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities is planned or ongoing
required_action: Develop and implement a comprehensive outsourcing policy
evidence: Document outlining the comprehensive outsourcing policy
verbatim_text: An intermediary seeking to outsource activities shall have in place a comprehensive policy to guide the assessment of whether and how those activities can be appropriately outsourced. The Board / partners (as the case may be) {hereinafter referred to as the “the Board”} of the intermediary shall have the responsibility for the outsourcing policy and related overall responsibility for activities undertaken under that policy. The policy shall cover activities or the nature of activities that can be outsourced, the authorities who can approve outsourcing of such activities, and the selection of third party to whom it can be outsourced. For example

title: Establish Outsourcing Policy
summary: Develop a policy for outsourcing activities that includes risk assessment and evaluation of risks.
required_action: Develop an outsourcing policy based on risk concentrations, limits on the overall level of outsourced activities, and other relevant factors.
evidence: Policy document outlining the criteria for outsourcing and risk management practices.
verbatim_text: For example, an activity shall not be outsourced if it would impair the supervisory authority’s right to assess, or its ability to supervise the business of the intermediary. The policy shall be based on an evaluation of risk concentrations, limits on the acceptable overall level of outsourced activities, risks arising from outsourcing multiple activities to the same entity, etc.

title: Regular Review of Outsourcing Policy
summary: Conduct regular reviews of the outsourcing policy in response to changes in the business environment.
required_action: Mandate a regular review of the outsourcing policy and ensure ongoing compliance with it.
evidence: Minutes or reports from policy reviews.
verbatim_text: The Board shall mandate a regular review of outsourcing policy for such activities in the wake of changing business environment. It shall also have overall responsibility for ensuring that all ongoing outsourcing decisions taken by the intermediary and the activities undertaken by the third-party, are in keeping with its outsourcing policy.

title: Consider Factors for Risk Assessment
summary: Evaluate various factors to determine the materiality of outsourcing risks.
required_action: Consider several factors in assessing the risk, including impact on financial performance, ability to cope with non-performance, regulatory status, and potential conflicts of interest.
evidence: Risk assessment report or documentation.
verbatim_text: The factors that could help in considering materiality in a risk management programme include- 2.1.1 The impact of failure of a third party to adequately perform the activity on the financial, reputational and operational performance of the intermediary and on the investors / clients; 2.1.2 Ability of the intermediary to cope up with the work, in case of non performance or failure by a third party by having suitable back-up arrangements; 2.1.3 Regulatory status of the third party, including its fitness and probity status; 2.1.4 Situations involving conflict of interest between the intermediary and the third party and the measures put in place by the intermediary to address such potential conflicts, etc.

title: Maintain Arm's Length Distance with Related Parties
summary: Ensure that a group entity or associate of the intermediary does not act as the third party while maintaining an arm's length distance.
required_action: Put in place systems to maintain an arm's length distance between the intermediary and the third party, including infrastructure, manpower, decision-making, record keeping, etc.
evidence: Documentation of systems put in place to ensure arm's length distance.
verbatim_text: While there shall not be any prohibition on a group entity / associate of the intermediary to act as the third party, systems shall be put in place to have an arm’s length distance between the intermediary and the third party in terms of infrastructure, manpower, decision-making, record keeping, etc. for avoidance of potential conflict of interests. Necessary disclosures in this regard shall be made as part of the contractual agreement.

title: Centralized Record Keeping
summary: Preserve records related to outsourced activities centrally for easy access and review.
required_action: Maintain central records of all outsourced activities that are readily accessible for review by the Board or senior management.
evidence: Centralized record-keeping system and documentation.
verbatim_text: The records relating to all activities outsourced shall be preserved centrally so that the same is readily accessible for review by the Board of the intermediary and / or its senior management, as and when needed. Such records shall be regularly updated and may also form part of the corporate governance review by the management of the intermediary.

title: Maintain and Update Records
summary: Investment Advisers shall maintain records of outsourcing arrangements as and when needed, which may also form part of the corporate governance review.
required_action: Maintain and update records regularly
evidence: Records maintained by the Investment Adviser
verbatim_text: Records shall be maintained and updated as and when needed. Such records may also form part of the corporate governance review by the management of the intermediary.

title: Ensure Fulfillment of Obligations
summary: Investment Advisers shall ensure that outsourcing arrangements do not diminish their ability to fulfill customer and regulatory obligations, nor impede effective supervision by regulators.
required_action: Ensure fulfillment of obligations
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with regulatory requirements
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall ensure that outsourcing arrangements neither diminish its ability to fulfill its obligations to customers and regulators, nor impede effective supervision by the regulators.

title: Full Liability for Outsourced Activities
summary: Investment Advisers shall be fully liable and accountable for activities outsourced to third parties as if they were provided in-house.
required_action: Be fully liable and accountable
evidence: Documentation of liability agreements with third parties
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall be fully liable and accountable for the activities that are being outsourced to the same extent as if the service were provided in-house.

title: Redress Losses Incurred by Investors
summary: Investment Advisers shall be liable for losses incurred by investors due to third party failures and responsible for redressing grievances.
required_action: Redress losses and grievances
evidence: Documentation of loss compensation and grievance resolution processes
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not affect the rights of an investor or client against the intermediary in any manner. The intermediary shall be liable to the investors for the loss incurred by them due to the failure of the third party and also be responsible for redressal of the grievances received from investors arising out of activities rendered by the third party.

title: Access to Outsourced Facilities/Premises/Data
summary: Investment Advisers shall have access to facilities, premises, and data used in outsourced activities.
required_action: Access to facilities, premises, and data
evidence: Documentation of access rights
verbatim_text: The facilities / premises / data that are involved in carrying out the outsourced activity by the service provider shall be deemed to be those of the registered intermediary. The intermediary itself and Regulator or the persons authorized by it shall have the right to access the same at any point of time.

title: Not Impair Supervision/Inspection
summary: Investment Advisers shall ensure that outsourcing arrangements do not impair the ability of SEBI/SRO or auditors to exercise regulatory responsibilities.
required_action: Ensure supervision/inspection is not impaired
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with supervisory requirements
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not impair the ability of SEBI/SRO or auditors to exercise its regulatory responsibilities such as supervision/inspection of the intermediary.

title: Conduct Due Diligence
summary: Investment Advisers shall conduct due diligence in selecting and monitoring third parties.
required_action: Conduct due diligence
evidence: Due diligence reports and records
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting the third party and in monitoring of its performance.

title: Exercise Due Care, Skill, and Diligence
summary: Investment Advisers shall exercise due care, skill, and diligence in selecting third parties.
required_action: Exercise due care, skill, and diligence
evidence: Due diligence reports and records
verbatim_text: It is important that the intermediary exercises due care, skill, and diligence in the selection of the third party to ensure that the third party has the ability and capacity to undertake the provision of the service effectively.

title: Assess Third Party’s Resources, Compatibility, Reputation, Concentration, and Foreign Environment
summary: Investment Advisers shall assess third party's resources, compatibility with their requirements, reputation, concentration of arrangements, and foreign environment.
required_action: Assess various factors
evidence: Due diligence reports and records
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: (a) third party’s resources and capabilities, including financial soundness, to perform the outsourcing work within the timelines fixed; (b) compatibility of the practices and systems of the third party with the intermediary’s requirements and objectives; (c) market feedback of the prospective third party’s business reputation and track record of their services rendered in the past; (d) level of concentration of the outsourced arrangements with a single third party; and (e) the environment of the foreign country where the third party is located.

title: Governing Outsourcing Arrangements by Written Contract
summary: Investment Advisers must have a written contract for outsourcing arrangements that clearly defines the rights, responsibilities and expectations of all parties involved.
required_action: Enter into a legally binding written contract with third-party service providers.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall be governed by a clearly defined and legally binding written contract between the intermediary and each of the third parties, the nature and detail of which shall be appropriate to the materiality of the outsourced activity in relation to the ongoing business of the intermediary. Care shall be taken to ensure that the outsourcing contract: (a) clearly defines what activities are going to be outsourced, including appropriate service and performance levels; (b) provides for mutual rights, obligations and responsibilities of the intermediary and the third party, including indemnity by the parties; (c) provides for the liability of the third party to the intermediary for unsatisfactory performance/other breach of the contract; (d) provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Clear Definition of Outsourced Activities
summary: Investment Advisers must clearly define what activities are being outsourced, including the service and performance levels.
required_action: Define in writing the specific activities to be outsourced along with appropriate service and performance levels.
evidence: Written documentation of the defined outsourcing activities.
verbatim_text: clearly defines what activities are going to be outsourced, including appropriate service and performance levels;

title: Mutual Rights, Obligations, and Responsibilities

required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions for mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities of the intermediary and third party, including indemnity by the parties.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts with relevant clauses highlighted.
verbatim_text: provides for mutual rights, obligations and responsibilities of the intermediary and the third party, including indemnity by the parties;

title: Liability for Unsatisfactory Performance
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the outsourcing contract includes provisions for liability of the third party in case of unsatisfactory performance.
required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions for the liability of the third party to the intermediary for unsatisfactory performance or other breach of the contract.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts with relevant clauses highlighted.
verbatim_text: provides for the liability of the third party to the intermediary for unsatisfactory performance/other breach of the contract;

title: Continuous Monitoring and Assessment
summary: Investment Advisers must continuously monitor and assess the third-party service providers to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory obligations.
required_action: Ensure continuous monitoring and assessment of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, enabling the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing.
evidence: Documentation of regular monitoring and assessment processes.
verbatim_text: provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Sub-contracting Provisions
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the outsourcing contract includes provisions for sub-contracting by third parties.

required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions addressing sub-contracting by the third party, ensuring that the intermediary maintains a similar level of control over risks.

verbatim_text: provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Confidentiality Clauses

required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract unambiguous confidentiality clauses to protect proprietary and customer data during and after the tenure of the contract.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts with relevant clauses highlighted.
verbatim_text: includes, where necessary, conditions of sub-contracting by the third-party, i.e. the contract shall enable intermediary to maintain a similar control over the risks when a third party outsources to further third parties as in the original direct outsourcing;

title: Preservation of Documents and Data
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the outsourcing contract includes provisions for the preservation of documents and data by third parties.
required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions for the preservation of documents and data by third parties.

required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from implementation of the outsourcing contract.

summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the outsourcing contract includes provisions for termination, termination rights, transfer of information, and exit strategies.
trigger: Outsourcing activities are conducted and need to be terminated
required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions for termination, termination rights, transfer of information, and exit strategies.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts with relevant clauses highlighted.
verbatim_text: provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Country Risk Management
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the outsourcing contract includes provisions addressing country risks, potential obstacles in exercising oversight, choice-of-law provisions, agreement covenants, and jurisdictional covenants.
trigger: Outsourcing activities are conducted to foreign third parties
required_action: Include in the outsourcing contract provisions addressing country risks, potential obstacles in exercising oversight, choice-of-law provisions, agreement covenants, and jurisdictional covenants.
evidence: Copies of the outsourcing contracts with relevant clauses highlighted.
verbatim_text: addresses additional issues arising from country risks and potential obstacles in exercising oversight and management of the arrangements when intermediary outsources its activities to foreign third party. For example, the contract shall include choice-of-law provisions and agreement covenants and jurisdictional covenants that provide for adjudication of disputes between the parties under the laws of a specific jurisdiction;

title: Establish and Maintain Contingency Plans
summary: Develop and maintain contingency plans, including disaster recovery plans, for each outsourcing arrangement.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties.
required_action: Establish and maintain specific contingency plans for each outsourcing arrangement, develop a plan for disaster recovery, and periodically test backup facilities.
evidence: Documentation of the established contingency plans, testing records, and reports.
verbatim_text:
6. The intermediary and its third parties shall establish and maintain contingency plans, including a plan for disaster recovery and periodic testing of backup facilities.
6.1. Specific contingency plans shall be separately developed for each outsourcing arrangement, as is done in individual business lines.

title: Develop Disaster Recovery Plans
summary: Develop and maintain disaster recovery plans to ensure business continuity.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties.
required_action: Develop a plan for disaster recovery as part of the contingency plans.
evidence: Documentation of the developed disaster recovery plan.
verbatim_text: 6. The intermediary and its third parties shall establish and maintain contingency plans, including a plan for disaster recovery and periodic testing of backup facilities.

title: Periodic Testing of Backup Facilities
summary: Conduct periodic tests to confirm the adequacy of third party’s systems.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties.
required_action: Periodically test critical security procedures and systems, and review backup facilities.
evidence: Records of periodic tests conducted and reports thereof.
verbatim_text: 6.4 Periodic tests of the critical security procedures and systems and review of the backup facilities shall be undertaken by the intermediary to confirm the adequacy of the third party’s systems.

title: Protect Confidential Information
summary: Ensure that confidential information is not disclosed to unauthorized persons.
required_action: Take appropriate steps to protect proprietary and confidential customer information, limit access of third party employees to data on a need-to-know basis, and ensure adequate checks and balances.
evidence: Documentation of measures taken to protect confidentiality, records of employee access controls, and reports thereof.
verbatim_text:
7. The intermediary shall take appropriate steps to require that third parties protect confidential information of both the intermediary and its customers from intentional or inadvertent disclosure to unauthorised persons.
7.1. An intermediary that engages in outsourcing is expected to take appropriate steps to protect its proprietary and confidential customer information and ensure that it is not misused or misappropriated.
7.2. The intermediary shall prevail upon the third party to ensure that the employees of the third party have limited access to the data handled and only on a “need to know” basis and the third party shall have adequate checks and balances to ensure the same.
